---
argmap-version: 0.2
title: "Tutorial: undercutting an undercut"
description: "t4's map with one more line: an answer to the undercut. Since `~$id` is banned, an attack on an evidence is never written by negating it. The one well-formed shape takes the undercut as a premise and concludes AGAINST what it concluded, which reads as `granted that objection, here is why it still fails to carry`. The same schema that wrote the undercut writes the answer to the undercut, and would write the answer to that, indefinitely: the ladder is one rule applied repeatedly, not four relation types. The shape is live on the flagship map at $resp-antitech, and this file is the isolated version of it."
---

# ===========================================================================
# THE SHAPE, and there is only one:
#
#     step       $s   q  @claim | @grounds
#     undercut   $u   q ~@claim | @obj-grounds AND $s
#     answer     $a   q  @claim | @ans-grounds AND $u
#
# Every rung takes the rung below it as a premise and concludes against what
# that rung concluded. Nothing new is learned at rung three; if you can read
# t4 you can read a ladder of any height.
#
# WHY IT IS THE ONLY SHAPE. `~$id` is a parse error (E3): an evidence is not
# a proposition, so there is nothing there to negate. What you want to say
# is "granted that this objection is in force, here is why it still does not
# carry", and that is a condition, so the objection goes on the premise side
# and the answer's own conclusion goes back to the original claim.
#
# LIVE INSTANCE, so this is not a toy shape invented for a tutorial. On
# experiments/llm-extraction/iabied-comprehensive-en.argmap:
#
#   $uc-antitech    0.15? ~@shutdown | @c12-antitech AND $shutdown-fine
#   $resp-antitech [opposing one lethal technology isn't anti-technology]
#                   0.9?  @shutdown | @c12-pro-tech AND $uc-antitech
#
# $resp-antitech is exactly the third line of the schema above. Ring it in
# the viewer with relation labels on and the words say so.
#
# WHAT THE ANSWER IS WORTH, and it is less than authors expect: an undercut
# of an undercut reinstates the claim only TOWARDS where it would have stood
# with the objection absent, never past it. It cancels an inhibitor; it does
# not add a reason. If the answer also carries a positive fact that bears on
# the claim in its own right, that fact needs its own ordinary evidence line
# beside this one.
# ===========================================================================

# ---- rungs 1 and 2, identical to t4-one-undercut --------------------------

@prints [The suspect's prints are on the inside of the window frame] 0.9:
@guilty [The suspect broke in on the night of the theft]:  # check: 0.6
$prints-ev [prints inside the frame put a hand on the window] 0.8 @guilty | @prints:

@visited [The suspect was invited into the studio a week earlier] 0.6:
$uc [an invited visit leaves the same prints] 0.7 ~@guilty | @visited AND $prints-ev:

# ---- rung 3: the answer ---------------------------------------------------
# Read the line as a sentence. Granted the visit, and granted that a visit
# would ordinarily explain the prints: the frame was painted shut until the
# morning of the theft, so prints from last week could not be on it.
#
# @sealed is the answer's own ground and it is a frontier root, so it keeps
# its pin. $resp takes $uc as a premise, which is what makes it an answer to
# the objection rather than a second reason for the claim.

@sealed [The frame was painted shut until the morning of the theft] 0.7:
$resp [prints from last week would be under the paint] 0.8 @guilty | @sealed AND $uc:

# ---- the ladder, read off the solve ---------------------------------------
# Solved 2026-08-04 (D36 defaults, solve_map.py, with --override standing in
# for a reader's own handles). Three states of the same file:
#
#   @guilty, check 0.60
#     objection unanswered   ($resp off)          0.680
#     objection answered     (as written)         0.763
#     objection never raised ($uc and $resp off)  0.851
#
# Read the three in that order. The answer is worth 0.083, and the objection
# it answers cost 0.171, so the claim ends up strictly between where it was
# with the objection standing and where it would have been had nobody raised
# it. THAT CEILING IS THE POINT: an answer to an objection cancels an
# inhibitor, and cancelling an inhibitor cannot take you past the argument
# you already had. An author who expects rung three to push the claim higher
# than rung one has mistaken an answer for a reason.
#
# The readout says the same thing structurally: $resp reports one P(U) row,
# exactly like $uc, because it compiles the same way. It is an inhibitor of
# an inhibitor, not a supporter of the claim, even though it is written with
# @guilty on its conclusion side.
#
# Where to go next: the corpus has this ladder at scale in
# examples/06-policy-tradeoff (two undercuts and a rebuttal in one map) and
# in examples/05-instrumental-convergence, whose section 4 contrasts the
# three objection kinds in six lines.
